Asymptotic safety (Weinberg's program).value: Asymptotic safety concept first proposed by Weinberg 1976 (unpublished lecture); term 'asymptotic safety' and formal framework published in Weinberg, 'Ultraviolet divergences in quantum theories of gravitation', in General Relativity: An Einstein Centenary Survey, eds. Hawking & Israel, Cambridge UP, 1979

Bryce DeWitt & John Archibald Wheeler.value: Wheeler-DeWitt equation paper: written 1966, published Physical Review 160:1113, August 1967 — ~1 year lag. Naming dispute: DeWitt called it 'Einstein-Schrodinger equation' attributing it to Wheeler for ~20 years; standard name 'Wheeler-DeWitt equation' settled at Osgood Hill conference 1988

General Relativity (Einstein 1915).value: General relativity had slow adoption 1915-1930s: initial experimental confirmation limited to Mercury perihelion (fitted) and 1919 Eddington light-bending. Full adoption by mainstream physics community took ~20 years (1915-1935). Second major adoption wave: post-1960 'Golden Age of GR' with development of black holes, neutron stars, cosmology

Gerard 't Hooft & Martinus Veltman.value: 't Hooft-Veltman one-loop QG with matter: Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré 20:69 (1974) — ~1 year after first announcement at conference 1973. Goroff-Sagnotti two-loop: submitted and published Physics Letters B 160:81, October 1985 (letter); full Nucl. Phys. B 266:709, 1986

Holographic principle -> AdS/CFT -> 'spa.value: AdS/CFT correspondence published: Maldacena arXiv hep-th/9711200, November 1997; published in Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics vol. 2, 1998. Exceeded 20,000 citations by ~2020 — among the most cited papers in theoretical physics history

Matvei Petrovich Bronstein.value: Arrested by NKVD August 1937 during Stalin's Great Purge; sentenced and executed 1938-02-18; work on quantum gravity neglected for ~50 years thereafter

Bronstein's 1936 papers: 'Quantentheorie schwacher Gravitationsfelder' published Phys. Z. Sowjetunion 9(2-3):140-157 (1936); 'Kvantovanie gravitatsionnykh voln' published JETP 6:195-236 (1936); work then effectively dormant until Gorelik-Frenkel biography 1994 (English ed.) reconstructed it — ~58 year propagation gap

Penrose spin networks / SU(2) recoupling.value: Spin networks revived by Rovelli-Smolin 1988-1990 as basis states of LQG — dormancy ended

Penrose spin networks / SU(2) recoupling.value: Spin networks invented by Penrose ~1964 as handwritten manuscript; first published 1971 in 'Angular momentum: an approach to combinatorial space-time', in Quantum Theory and Beyond, ed. T. Bastin, Cambridge University Press, pp. 151-180

Quantum gravity (sought / conjectured —.value: Quantum gravity program broadly: ~90 years (1916/1935-2026) without a consolidated theory — the longest-running fundamental unsolved problem in theoretical physics relative to its identified need. Field re-identified as urgent in 1984 (first superstring revolution) but no settled child to date

source.title: Quantum Gravity — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

Quantum gravity (sought / conjectured —.value: Non-renormalizability of quantum gravity ('t Hooft-Veltman 1974 with matter; Goroff-Sagnotti 1985-86 pure gravity two-loop) effectively closed the naive perturbative QG program, creating a decade-long dormancy 1970-1983 and redirecting effort toward string theory and later LQG

source.title: Quantum gravity at two loops — ADS (Goroff-Sagnotti Phys Lett B 1985)

Quantum gravity (sought / conjectured —.value: 'Quantum gravity' as a phrase: graviton term coined ~1934 by Blokhintsev and Galperin (JETP 1934); 'quantum gravity' as a field name solidified in English literature by ~1950s-1960s. Bronstein used 'Quantentheorie schwacher Gravitationsfelder' (quantum theory of weak gravitational fields) 1936

Nobel shared with Genzel and Ghez.

proposed:LHC-SUSY-non-detection.value: LHC Higgs boson discovered at ~125 GeV, announced 2012-07-04; no supersymmetric particles found at TeV scale through LHC Run 1 (2010-2012) and Run 2 (2015-2018) and Run 3 (2022-present). This absence is Bayesian dis-confirmation of many string/SUSY models

proposed:LIGO-GW150914-2015.value: LIGO first gravitational wave detection: GW150914 detected 2015-09-14 09:51 UTC; published Physical Review Letters 116:061102, February 12 2016. Binary black hole merger ~36+29 solar masses. Nobel Prize 2017 (Weiss, Barish, Thorne)

source.title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger — PRL 116:061102

proposed:QG-quantum-information-converge.value: Quantum gravity / quantum information convergence deepened 2020-2026: island formula, holographic quantum error correction, replica wormholes, ER=EPR. Workshop 'Recent Developments in Quantum Gravity and Applications to Cosmology and Black Hole Physics' scheduled Hangzhou, May 31 - June 5 2026

proposed:causal-set-theory.value: Causal set theory founded by Rafael Sorkin and collaborators; key paper: Bombelli-Lee-Meyer-Sorkin 'Space-Time as a Causal Set', Physical Review Letters 59(5):521-524, August 3 1987

proposed:contribution-share-GR-to-QG.value: ESTIMATE: GR contributes ~50% of the conceptual DNA of any proposed quantum gravity child — specifically: background-independence requirement (LQG line), the Einstein field equations as the IR limit constraint (all children), the black-hole entropy benchmark (all children), the graviton as spin-2 massless field (perturbative/string line). QM contributes the complementary ~50%: operator formalism, path integrals, renormalization methods.

'The Page curve of Hawking radiation from semiclassical geometry', JHEP 03 (2020) 149 (arXiv:1908.10996). Dominant development in black-hole QG 2019-2024
